events.title: Uptown Royalty
events.summary: Latin, Jazz, Dance
events.description: Latin, Jazz, Dance

meta.og_description: Latin, Jazz, Dance

detail_page_data.location_detail: Charles A. Dana Discovery Center The Harlem Meer Performance Festival is back with a fresh new lineup! Join the Central Park Conservancy on August 9, 2026, for a performance by Latin music husband-and-wife duo Uptown Royalty. MEET THE ARTIST: A Q&A WITH UPTOWN ROYALTY How would you describe your music or performance style? Uptown Royalty delivers a dynamic, genre-defying fusion of salsa, R&B, and jazz, creating a sound that is both timeless and electrifying. Founded by Bronx native Jodi Music and her husband, Washington Heights native Ron Renaissance, the band was built on a shared vision to craft unforgettable live music experiences that move audiences emotionally and physically. What does a live audience feel, hear, or experience when they see you perform? More than a performance, Uptown Royalty creates an immersive experience. We sing, play live instruments, and dance, bringing high-energy showmanship and authentic musicianship to every stage. Our connection with the audience transforms each event into a celebration, where rhythm, soul, and passion come alive. Audiences don’t just hear our music, they feel it. From the pulse of Latin percussion to the smooth soulfulness of R&B and the improvisational spirit of jazz, Uptown Royalty delivers a vibrant, engaging performance that leaves a lasting impression. Being a husband-and-wife band that also performs with our close friends makes this band extra special. We are rooted in love, and you can feel that from the moment you hear us. What inspires your work? Our work is inspired by all of our stories growing up in NYC and being kids in music programs. We were raised by after-school music programs and we never forget where we came from—it’s a big part of who we are. Rooted in the rich cultural heartbeat of New York City, our performances celebrate diversity, rhythm, and soul. We don’t just perform, we ignite the stage. With powerful vocals, vibrant choreography, and high-energy musicianship, we captivate audiences of all backgrounds and transform every festival into a celebration of life, love, and family—something we feel very strongly about, especially with the climate of the world today. What is the connection between your work and the Harlem community? Jodi Music is from the Bronx and Ron Renaissance is from Washington Heights, but we have collaborated with the National Jazz Museum in Harlem, Harlem Nights Festivals, the Victoria in Harlem, the New York City Marathon in Harlem—performing for the runners—and love Harlem very much! We’ve also performed at Melba’s summer block parties and at Red Rooster, where we began our relationship over eight years ago. Harlem is home for us! ABOUT THE HARLEM MEER PERFORMANCE FESTIVAL The Harlem Meer Performance Festival is a beloved annual tradition, filling Central Park with music and movement on select Sundays throughout the summer. The festival is free, and all ages are welcome. Check out our Event FAQs for more information and join our mailing list to receive event updates. COMMUNITY EVENTS BY THE CENTRAL PARK CONSERVANCY Central Park Conservancy community events reflect the spirit of the Park itself: fun, free, and open to all. Join us all year for family-friendly programs across Central Park—featuring music, movement, art, film, and more—creating a culture of connection in the Park we all love. See All Upcoming Events

detail_page_data.location_detail: Chess & Checkers House Chess & Checkers House (mid-Park at 64th Street) Saturday, August 15 Start: 11:00 am Join Grandmaster Michael Rohde for a 30-minute lecture, followed by a simul. Register to Attend Michael Rohde is a former junior chess champion, having been rated as a master at 13. He gained the International Master title in 1976, followed by that of Grandmaster in 1988. At one point, he was ranked as high as 59th in the world. In recent years, Rohde has played in many tournaments in NYC’s Marshall Chess Club. He won the Marshall Chess Club Championship in 1990 and 1994, and tied for first in 2012. This event is free and open to players ages 6 and up. Register in advance to secure your spot. Registration opens one month prior to each scheduled program date. Participation is limited to 30 players. A limited number of walk-up spaces will be available on a first-come-first-served basis. Prior chess experience is required to participate. Beginners are welcome to watch.

Alex Ramirez is a Colombian saxophonist, composer, producer, and educator based in New York City. events.summary: Jazz, Soul, Latin, World, Dance
events.description: Jazz, Soul, Latin, World, Dance

meta.og_description: Jazz, Soul, Latin, World, Dance

detail_page_data.location_detail: Charles A. Dana Discovery Center The Harlem Meer Performance Festival is back with a fresh new lineup! Join the Central Park Conservancy on August 23, 2026, for a performance by salsa and Latin jazz ensemble the Ray Delgado Project. MEET THE ARTIST: A Q& A WITH THE RAY DELGADO PROJECT How would you describe your music or performance style? Led by percussionist Ray Delgado, our group features seven talented musicians on vibraphone, piano, bass, bongos, congas, timbales, and vocals, delivering a rich and authentic Latin sound rooted in New York’s musical tradition. I’d describe it as high-energy, rhythm-driven salsa with a strong live feel. What does a live audience feel, hear, or experience when they see you perform? The band connects directly with the audience—whether they’re dancers, listeners, or both. It’s not just about playing songs; it’s about creating a shared experience, where the rhythm builds, and the energy rises. What makes the Ray Delgado Project memorable is the connection—between the rhythm, the band, and the audience. The rhythm section locks in deep, creating that pulse that dancers feel immediately, while the arrangements breathe and evolve in real time. There’s a sense that the music is happening with the audience, not just for them. What inspires your work? I’m deeply inspired by the tradition of salsa and Latin jazz, but also by the idea of finding my own voice within it. I respect the masters, those who came before me and even after me, the sound of the streets, the dance floors, the barrios of the world. I love to keep our traditions going, that Afro-Caribbean sound mixed with the jazz of our African American roots. What is the connection between your work and the Harlem community? Harlem is my home. My music is my connection to all of Harlem. From Chick Webb to Tito Puente, from swing to bebop, and from mambo to cha-cha, this is where it all began for me. My work is deeply connected to Harlem because Harlem represents history, migration, and cultural exchange—the same forces that shape my music. That blend of rhythms, languages, and stories lives inside the music I play. ABOUT THE HARLEM MEER PERFORMANCE FESTIVAL The Harlem Meer Performance Festival is a beloved annual tradition, filling Central Park with music and movement on select Sundays throughout the summer. The festival is free, and all ages are welcome. Check out our Event FAQs for more information and join our mailing list to receive event updates. detail_page_data.location_detail: 110th Street & Malcolm X Boulevard June 20– October 31 Saturdays, 10:00 am–7:00 pm Location: Farmers’ Gate Entrance 110th Street & Malcolm X Boulevard Beginning Saturday, June 20, 2026, the Central Park Conservancy and Unity Market NY are proud to launch a new farm stand at 110th Street and Malcolm X Boulevard, at the historic Farmers’ Gate entrance to Central Park. Nestled just inside the Park, overlooking the Harlem Meer and steps from the new Davis Center, this vibrant destination serves as a gathering place for food, community, and culture. Rooted in a shared belief that exceptional food should be both accessible and community-centered, this collaboration features: Abundant fresh produce (eligible for purchase with SNAP/EBT) Seasonal food offerings Curated household provisioning Educational programming All offerings are curated by Chef Russell Jackson, Operator and Culinary Cultural Strategist for ReverenceNYC Hospitality Group. Together, the Central Park Conservancy and Unity Market NY are building an innovative model that blends premium food experiences with public purpose—bringing culinary excellence, seasonal offerings, and meaningful food access to Harlem and the broader New York City community.

detail_page_data.location_detail: Blockhouse See inside Central Park’s oldest surviving structure! Located on a prominent rock outcrop in the North Woods, the Blockhouse was part of a fortification system built to defend New York from the British during the War of 1812. For one day only, join Open House New York and the Central Park Conservancy to explore the Blockhouse and learn about the history of the site with the Conservancy’s expert guides.

events.title: Founders’ Day: 200th Anniversary of Seneca Village
events.summary: Join the Central Park Conservancy for a music-filled service at AME Zion Church in Harlem to honor the 200th anniversary of the first land purchase in Seneca Village.
events.description: Join the Central Park Conservancy for a music-filled service at AME Zion Church in Harlem to honor the 200th anniversary of the first land purchase in Seneca Village.

meta.og_title: Founders’ Day: 200th Anniversary of Seneca Village
meta.og_description: Join the Central Park Conservancy for a music-filled service at AME Zion Church in Harlem to honor the 200th anniversary of the first land purchase in…

schema_org.description: Join the Central Park Conservancy for a music-filled service at AME Zion Church in Harlem to honor the 200th anniversary of the first land purchase in Seneca Village.
schema_org.name: Founders’ Day: 200th Anniversary of Seneca Village

detail_page_data.location_detail: Mother AME Zion Church, 140 West 137th Street, New York, NY 10030 200 years ago, on September 17, 1825, congregant Andrew Williams and the trustees of the AME Zion Church were among the first to purchase land in the area between West 82nd and 89th Streets, which would become Seneca Village. On Sunday, September 14, join the Central Park Conservancy for a music-filled service at the historic AME Zion Church in Harlem—the first Black church in New York City—to honor this significant anniversary (in collaboration with the James L. Varick Community Center, Inc.). Through the sermon, live music, and a conversation with historians, discover the communal roots of this thriving, predominantly African-American 19th-century community. Service will begin at 11:00 AM, followed by a discussion between AME Zion Church leaders and a Seneca Village historian. Members of the Institute for the Exploration of Seneca Village History and the Envisioning Seneca Village team will also be present to answer questions about their research. Light refreshments will be available after service. Event Schedule Church Service: 11:00 AM Refreshments / Open House: 12:30 PM–1:00 PM Dabney N. Montgomery Heritage Center (AME Zion History Museum) Institute for the Exploration of Seneca Village History Envisioning Seneca Village Discussion: 1:00 PM This event is part of Seneca Village: Toward a Permanent Commemoration , an ongoing program series funded by the Mellon Foundation. This series will culminate in a community-informed framework guiding the future design of a permanent commemoration of Seneca Village in Central Park. Join the Seneca Village mailing list to receive event news, Seneca Village history, and more! Sign Up

events.title: Before, there was Seneca Village!
events.summary: Watch as Seneca Village is brought to life through an interpretive performance.
events.description: Watch as Seneca Village is brought to life through an interpretive performance.

meta.og_description: Watch as Seneca Village is brought to life through an interpretive performance.

schema_org.description: Watch as Seneca Village is brought to life through an interpretive performance.
schema_org.name: Before, there was Seneca Village!

detail_page_data.location_detail: Seneca Village Landscape Join us in the historic Seneca Village landscape in Central Park for a performance that takes you back to Seneca Village in 1845. Interpretive music, dance, and spoken word will bring to life a world where Black New Yorkers built their own homes, churches, and a school, exploring how Andrew Williams's and others’ 1825 land purchase evolved into a thriving community. Performances by: DeWitt Fleming, Jr., Broadway performer Alphonso Horne, musician Mikumari Caiyhe, spoken word artist Bring a blanket to sit on and enjoy the performance in comfort! The Seneca Village landscape is between West 85th Street and West Drive. Enter the Park at West 85th Street. This event is part of Seneca Village: Toward a Permanent Commemoration , an ongoing program series funded by the Mellon Foundation. This series will culminate in a community-informed framework guiding the future design of a permanent commemoration of Seneca Village in Central Park. Join the Seneca Village mailing list to receive event news, Seneca Village history, and more! Email Address *
